newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president apologises over spending abuses.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president apologises over spending abuses.

text.p: South Korean president Kim Young-sam, seeking to defuse a political crisis and rescue his administration, on Friday apologised on live television over election campaign spending abuses.

But he again insisted it would be impossible to reveal details of his own spending in 1992 presidential elections. The opposition has alleged his campaign was partly bankrolled by the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group and far exceeded legal spending limits.

"Recently, the 1992 presidential election funds have been raised as a problem in political circles," Kim said on national television. "For this, first of all, I and our entire political circle must bow our heads to the public and repent of past wrongdoings."
But he added: "I'm sure you understand that it is impossible to reveal the entire size of funds and spending from five years ago during a hectic election campaign."

Kim, whose credibility has been shattered by the furore over campaign spending and a separate bribery scandal involving senior aides and his own son, called on all political parties to draw up new legislation to combat campaign spending irregularities.
Kim's earlier refusal to detail his campaign spending, in comments relayed through a top aide last week, sparked public outrage and veiled calls for his resignation.
